BiblicalUsage: The sceptre is the rod of empire, and in Esther it is the difference between life and death. Whoever comes into the inner court uncalled has one law: to be put to death, except the king hold out the golden sceptre. He held it out to Esther twice, and she touched the top of it and lived.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the golden sceptre is grace made visible. The law said death, the king's hand said live, and I hold that God still holds out His sceptre to those who come uncalled.
